# Headlight trim and lens tinting

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Remove front bumper and headlights, heat lenses in a 215 degree oven for 15 minutes to tint or paint trim. [t851]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Remove the front bumper.
2. Disconnect the lighting harnesses.
3. Unbolt the headlights from the vehicle.
4. Unscrew the fasteners on the back of each headlight housing.
5. Preheat an oven to 215 degrees.
6. [Partial] Heat the headlights in the oven for 15 minutes.
7. Wear gloves and gently pull the lens away from its housing, avoiding the caulking seal.
8. Remove the screws securing the chrome trim into the lens.
9. Paint the chrome trim with your desired color.
10. Tint the side marker lights if you wish to do so optionally.
11. Wait for the paint on the trim to dry completely.
12. Reinsert the tinted or painted side marker lenses back into their housings.
13. Place the trimmed lens assembly back inside its housing.
14. [Partial] Heat the reassembled headlight in the oven at 215 degrees for another 15 minutes.
15. Reinstall the headlights onto your Xterra.

_Procedure reported by [t851]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/diy-paint-the-inside-of-youre-headlights-w-pics.3448/>_

## Tools

- [Partial] Oven [t851]
- [Partial] Gloves [t851]

## Tips & gotchas

- Ensure the caulking seal remains intact during lens removal for a proper reseal. [t851]
